steps.tx: **Crohn disease** is an idiopathic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any segment of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus in a discontinuous fashion, characterized by classical **skip lesions**. The inflammation is inherently **transmural**, extending through the mucosal, submucosal, muscularis propria, and subserosal layers. This transmural depth underlies the propensity of Crohn disease to form deep penetrating fissures, intra-abdominal sinus tracts, strictures, and internal fistulae.

left.title: Crohn Disease
points: Anatomical extent: Pan-enteric (mouth to anus)
Distribution: Discontinuous 'skip lesions'
Depth of inflammation: Transmural (full-thickness)
Complications: Fistulae, strictures, intra-abdominal abscesses

right.title: Ulcerative Colitis
points: Anatomical extent: Colon only (starts at rectum)
Distribution: Continuous mucosal involvement
Depth of inflammation: Mucosal and submucosal only
Complications: Toxic megacolon, severe mucosal bleeding

steps.tx: Endoscopic visualization of active intestinal inflammation reveals deep, sharp **serpiginous linear ulcers** separated by intervening areas of edematous mucosal inflammation and preserved islands of tissue, producing a classic **cobblestone appearance**. Unlike ulcerative colitis where the rectum is nearly always involved, the rectum is frequently spared in Crohn disease, and biopsy specimens taken from endoscopically normal-appearing skip areas often disclose early histological mucosal inflammation.

steps.tx: The pathognomonic histological hallmark of Crohn disease, present in up to thirty percent of endoscopic biopsy specimens, is the **non-caseating granuloma**. These discrete collections of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells occur within the lamina propria and submucosa, entirely devoid of central caseous necrosis. When identified, non-caseating granulomas definitively corroborate the diagnosis, although their absence does not exclude Crohn disease.

left.title: Crohn Disease Granulomas
points: Morphology: Microgranulomas, non-caseating
Distribution: Submucosal and lamina propria; small
Caseation: Completely absent
Location: May occur away from inflamed ulcers

right.title: Intestinal Tuberculosis Granulomas
points: Morphology: Large, confluent (> 400 microns)
Distribution: Dense submucosal aggregation
Caseation: Central caseous necrosis present
Acid-fast bacilli: Detectable on Ziehl-Neelsen stain or PCR

steps.tx: Perianal fistulizing complications develop in up to thirty percent of patients with Crohn disease. Clinical classification follows the American Gastroenterological Association criteria, categorizing fistulae into simple and **complex perianal fistula** phenotypes. Complex fistulae feature a high internal opening (above the dentate line), multiple external tracks, an associated perianal abscess, or a rectovaginal fistula. **Pelvic MRI** is the gold standard imaging modality for defining spatial anatomy and guiding therapy.

rows: Low tract, single external opening, no abscess
High tract, multiple tracks, abscess, or rectovaginal
EUA with loose non-cutting seton plus Infliximab
Pelvic MRI (T2 fat-suppressed) and endoanal US
Precise delineation of sphincter complex involvement

steps.tx: Primary therapeutic induction for moderate-to-severe luminal and fistulizing Crohn disease utilizes monoclonal anti-TNF antibodies. The humanized chimeric monoclonal antibody **infliximab** is administered as an intravenous induction regimen at **5** mg/kg given at weeks **0**, **2**, and **6**, followed by 5 mg/kg maintenance infusions every 8 weeks. Infliximab binds both soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha, inducing enterocyte apoptosis, closing complex fistulae, and achieving durable deep endoscopic mucosal healing.

steps.tx: Long-standing transmural terminal ileal inflammation commonly results in fibrostenotic intestinal luminal narrowing. Cross-sectional enterography displays circumferential mural thickening, submucosal fibrosis, and proximal pre-stenotic bowel dilatation, producing the classical **string sign of Kantor** on barium studies. When localized fibrotic strictures cause recurrent mechanical obstructive symptoms without active penetrating inflammation, **strictureplasty** (such as Heineke-Mikulicz) is performed to preserve bowel length.

left.title: Strictureplasty (Heineke-Mikulicz / Finney)
points: Indication: Short-segment fibrotic strictures (< 10 cm)
Principle: Longitudinal incision and transverse closure
Advantage: Preserves total bowel length and absorptive surface
Contraindication: Active perforation or suspected malignancy

right.title: Segmental Resection
points: Indication: Long-segment strictures or multiple close strictures
Principle: Resection of diseased segment and primary anastomosis
Disadvantage: Cumulative loss of bowel length risks short bowel syndrome
Requirement: Essential if malignancy cannot be excluded

steps.tx: Extensive terminal ileal involvement or surgical ileocolic resection severely reduces the enterohepatic circulation of bile salts. Depletion of the circulating bile acid pool impairs intraluminal micellar solubilization of dietary lipids, causing severe **fat malabsorption**. Unabsorbed luminal fatty acids avidly chelate free intraluminal calcium, leaving dietary oxalate unbound and freely absorbed in the colon, which dramatically promotes hyperoxaluria and recurrent **calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis**.

nodes.label: Terminal ileal resection (> 50 cm) or inflammation
Impaired bile salt reabsorption and fat malabsorption
Free fatty acids chelate intraluminal calcium
Unbound oxalate absorbed in colon -> Calcium oxalate stones

steps.tx: The **Montreal classification** stratifies Crohn disease into distinct phenotypic categories to guide prognostic expectations and therapeutic planning. Patients are categorized based on age at diagnosis (A1 below **17**, A2 between **17** and **40**, A3 above **40** years), primary anatomical location (L1 ileal, L2 colonic, L3 ileocolonic, L4 isolated upper disease), and dominant disease behaviour: **B1** non-stricturing non-penetrating, **B2** stricturing, and **B3** penetrating disease.

Patients are categorized based on age at diagnosis: A1 below 17, A2 between 17 and 40, and A3 above 40 years. Anatomical location is classified as L1 ileal, L2 colonic, L3 ileocolonic, and L4 isolated upper disease. Dominant disease behaviour is classified as B1 non-stricturing non-penetrating, B2 stricturing, and B3 penetrating disease.

rows: Terminal ileum / Colon / Ileocolon / Isolated upper GI
